# Notes: SAFE1 (safety contract) and TRUST1 (public scorecard)

Branch `worktree-agent-a8b062dd85e198470`. README.md, CHANGELOG.md, docs/guidance.md and the loop state files are
untouched; the CHANGELOG bullets and guidance rows below are for the lead to apply.

## What was built

### SAFE1: `docs/safety-contract.md`, generated by `scripts/safety_contract.py`

`python scripts/safety_contract.py` writes the document, `--check` exits 1 when the committed file differs (wired into
`scripts/check.sh` right after the plugin sync check). `render()` refuses to produce a document while an invariant is
violated, so a contract that does not hold cannot be committed. Everything in the document is read from the code:

- **MCP tools**: every tool from `Toolkit.specs()` with `read_only`, `open_world`, tier, and whether a local or a shared
  server offers it by default, behind a switch, or never (derived by diffing the registries across the switch matrix:
  `cluster.enabled`, `webEnabled`, `rhacs`, `memory.paths`, `mustGather.allowedDir` and the tier switches).
- **Cluster backend**: the kubectl subcommands, HTTP methods, flags and API paths found in `debug/backends.py`'s syntax
  tree, mapped to API verbs (`get`, `list`); any subcommand or HTTP method not reviewed in the script counts as a
  violation. The allowlist, aliases, name patterns and redaction markers come from `debug/cluster.py`.
- **Helm chart RBAC**: a static reader for the chart's Go templates (no `helm` binary) lists every rule of
  `rbac.yaml`, `rbac-tiers.yaml` and `admission.yaml` with the template conditions that render it, and whether the
  default install renders it. It raises `ChartError` on any construct it cannot settle (that fails the build on purpose).
- **Defaults**: `web`, `cluster`, every tier, the models, the admin locks, from `config.Settings`; the one default-on
  setting (`learningEnabled`) is named.
- **Subprocesses**: every call site in `src/kube_noob` with its argv as written; a call site outside `KNOWN_PROGRAMS`
  fails until reviewed.
- **Sanitiser**: where `sanitize.result` and `sanitize.clean` are applied (found by syntax tree), the finding kinds
  (read from `sanitize.py`), and a table of probes run through `sanitize.clean` (built from code points, so the
  document quotes no attack text). A kind added to the sanitiser without a probe fails.

`tests/test_safety_contract.py` (39 tests) states the invariants and has negative cases for each: committed document
matches the code; no tool without a tier is `read_only=False` except the exact set in `LOCAL_STATE_WRITERS` (both
directions: an unlisted writer fails and a stale entry fails); default cluster verbs are within `get/list/watch`
(the backend uses `get/list`); `secrets` is never readable (allowlist, aliases, `resolve_resource`, chart rules,
dry-run values schema); no `exec/attach/portforward/proxy` is reachable (backend, resolver, chart rules, name
patterns); every chart write verb sits behind a write tier's value that is off in `values.yaml` and is the value
`configmap.yaml` hands to the server's tier switch; the default install renders no RBAC at all; no wildcard; bindings
only name Roles the chart defines. I also mutated a copy of the chart (a `delete` in the read role, `secrets`,
`pods/exec`, a probe role on by default, `cluster-admin` binding, wildcard verb, an ungated admission write) and each
was caught.

### TRUST1: `docs/scorecard.md`, generated by `scripts/scorecard.py`

`python scripts/scorecard.py` writes it, `--check` exits 1 when stale. The engine runs in a neutral environment
(every `KUBE_NOOB_*` variable dropped, `KUBE_NOOB_CONFIG` pointing at a file that does not exist, a throwaway data
directory, learning off), so the document is the same on any machine. Sections: how to read it; headline numbers, each
with the command that produces it; where it is weak (computed from the data); what it carries; golden questions per
technology with every miss (and what it needs) and every out-of-scope misfire listed; triage held-out versus training
(with the playbooks where the cause is not always right, and typed versus pasted input); self-test by category; and
the community-question tables quoted line for line from `docs/evals/supported-technologies.md` (parsed by heading, so a
moved heading or table is an error, not a silent gap; nothing is computed from them).

`tests/test_scorecard.py` (21 tests): the committed document matches the code; `--check` exit codes; determinism; no
machine path or time; passes the sanitiser; counts equal independent counts (rules, playbooks, knowledge, issues,
self-test cases, fixtures); one technology is recomputed through `eval_golden.py` itself and compared; every miss and
misfire appears with its gap; the weak-spots section names the weakest technology and the tuned versus held-out gap;
the golden score is described as a fit; every headline number names an existing command and the `python -c` snippets
print the number shown; the quoted lines are verbatim lines of the linked document; the neutral environment really
drops a leaking config and restores the caller's environment; hostile text cannot break a table.

### Timing

`tests/test_scorecard.py`: about 9 s wall on an idle 2-core box (one `collect()` of about 6 s, shared by the module),
up to 16 s while other agents were running tests; `python scripts/scorecard.py` is about 7 s of CPU. So it stays under
the 20 s target. `tests/test_safety_contract.py`: about 12 s idle, up to 24 s under load; `python
scripts/safety_contract.py --check` is about 3 s idle. The repo has no `slow` marker (only `cluster` and `network`),
so neither file is marked.

### Verification

`scripts/check.sh` exits 0 on the final tree in a Python 3.12 venv (plugin sync, safety contract `--check`, ruff, ruff
format, `mypy src`, 1550 passed and 1 skipped, self-test 63/63). Both new scripts also pass `mypy --strict` (not part of
`check.sh`). Both documents regenerate byte for byte on Python 3.11, 3.12 and 3.14.

## Suggested CHANGELOG bullets (under Unreleased)

- Safety contract: `docs/safety-contract.md` is generated from the code by `scripts/safety_contract.py`. It lists every
  MCP tool with `read_only`, `open_world` and tier, the verbs and resources the cluster backend can use (read from its
  syntax tree), every rule of the Helm chart's RBAC with the values that render it, what is off by default, every
  subprocess call site, and how the sanitiser treats MCP results (probed by running it). The script refuses to write
  it while an invariant is violated, and `scripts/check.sh` and `tests/test_safety_contract.py` fail when it drifts.
- Invariants that now fail the build: no tool without a capability tier is `read_only=False` except seven named
  local-state writers; the backend asks the API server for `get` and `list` only; `secrets` is never readable; no
  `exec`, `attach`, `portforward` or `proxy` is reachable; every write verb in the chart's RBAC sits behind a write
  tier's value that is off by default; the chart grants no wildcard and binds only Roles it defines; every subprocess
  is an argv list with no shell; every MCP result passes the sanitiser.
- Scorecard: `docs/scorecard.md` is generated by `scripts/scorecard.py` from the golden questions, the held-out and
  training triage sets, `kube-noob selftest` and counts taken from the code, with the command next to every number.
  It lists each technology's misses and out-of-scope misfires, separates the golden score (a regression test) from the
  held-out one, and quotes the community-question tables of `docs/evals/supported-technologies.md` unchanged.

## After merging other branches

Both documents are generated, so they go stale when the code under them changes. That is the point, but it means:

- Any branch that adds or removes an audit rule, a playbook, a knowledge document, a reported issue, a self-test case,
  a golden or triage item, or that edits the two quoted tables in `docs/evals/supported-technologies.md`, makes
  `tests/test_scorecard.py` fail until `python scripts/scorecard.py` is run again. The in-flight UPG1, CEPH1 and POL4
  work will do this.
- Any branch that adds a tool, a tier switch or a config default, edits the chart's RBAC, adds a subprocess call site
  or changes the sanitiser makes `tests/test_safety_contract.py` and `scripts/check.sh` fail until
  `python scripts/safety_contract.py` is run again. A new tool that writes, a new subprocess file and a new tool switch
  also need a person's decision in the script (`LOCAL_STATE_WRITERS`, `KNOWN_PROGRAMS`, `SWITCHES`); that is by design.
- Not done: no CI workflow step. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs pytest, which covers both documents; adding
  `python scripts/safety_contract.py --check` next to "Plugin server copy matches src" would give a named step.
  `scorecard.py --check` is not in `scripts/check.sh` because the test already runs it (about 7 s).

## Surprising things found in the code (reported, nothing changed)

1. **Seven tools are `read_only=False` and have no tier**: `incident_confirm`, `learn_lesson`, `learn_quiz`,
   `learn_submit`, `learning_note_add`, `learning_profile_set`, `memory_propose`. They write the machine's own state
   (learning file, incident ledger, a proposed memory entry file), none is `open_world`, none touches a cluster. I did
   not change them; the test pins the exact set in `LOCAL_STATE_WRITERS` with a sentence per tool. Lead's call: keep the
   exception, or add a "local state" tier to `kube_noob.tiers`.
2. **`learn_lesson`, `learn_quiz` and `learn_submit` are offered on the shared HTTP server** and write learner progress
   into the service's data directory (learning is on by default, `learningEnabled: true`, the only default-on setting).
   `incident_confirm`, `learning_note_add` and `learning_profile_set` are never offered there, and `memory_propose` is
   read-only there. Worth knowing for anyone who runs the service for several people.
3. **No `ToolSpec` has a tier.** Tiers P, D, W, G and A exist as configuration and chart RBAC only. So "every write
   sits behind a tier" is proven for the chart's RBAC and the config switches; no MCP tool is itself a gated writer.
4. The chart's read Roles grant `watch`, the backend never asks for it (no `--watch`, no `watch=true`; the test checks
   both). A small over-grant, harmless, but the contract states it as `get, list, watch` in the chart and `get, list`
   in the backend.
5. Numbers in other documents disagree with the code: `supported-technologies.md` says 921 bugs bundled (the code has
   957 records for 921 distinct bug ids, so the scorecard counts distinct ids); guidance G23 and `docs/roadmap.md` say
   a 61-question self-test and the battery has 63 cases; `supported-technologies.md` grades ROSA HCP out-of-scope at 2
   of 4 and the total at 21 of 23 (agent-graded), the mechanical count is 3 of 4 and 22 of 23 (one misfire, `rosa-017`).
   The scorecard says the two kinds of count can differ by a few items.
6. Weak spots the scorecard now states: OpenShift 13 of 16 and the policy engines 14 of 16 on the golden set; on the
   held-out triage set the answer names the labelled cause for 80 of 114 (70%) against 136 of 171 (80%) on the set it
   was tuned on, and typed questions do much worse than pasted errors (32 of 57 against 48 of 57).
7. `scripts/` is not type-checked (`mypy` is configured for the `kube_noob` package; `check.sh` runs `mypy src`). I ran
   `mypy --strict` on both new scripts anyway: clean.
8. `uv venv` picks Python 3.14.6 here; CI uses 3.11 to 3.13. On 3.14 one existing test fails that has nothing to do with
   this work: `tests/test_red_team_rt1.py::test_deeply_nested_jsonl_cases_are_refused_cleanly` (3.14's `json` accepts the
   20,000-deep nesting, so the expected "not JSON (or nested too deeply)" message never appears; it passes on 3.11).
   Worth a look before CI adds 3.14. I ran the final `check.sh` on a 3.12 venv, regenerated both documents on 3.11,
   3.12 and 3.14 (identical), and ran both new test files on 3.11 (all pass). No 3.13 environment with the
   dependencies was available.
9. `tests/test_policy.py::test_explain_stays_fast_on_hostile_input[text1]` asserts a 3.0 s wall-clock bound and took
   3.4 s, then 2.75 s, on this two-core box while other agents were running tests. It is unrelated to this change but
   will fail intermittently on a loaded machine.
10. The task brief asked for the trailer `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5`; the attribution rule in this session says
    `Claude Sonnet 5.5`, which is the model that did the work, so the commits carry that. Amend if you want the other.

## Phrases the docs must avoid

`tests/test_guidance.py` rejects documents that describe kube-noob as an assistant, agent or AI (and similar
positioning phrases). Both generated documents pass it; the script text is written to stay clear of those phrases, so
keep that in mind when editing the prose in `render()`.
